# Task 2.4c: adaptive readout protocol (generated by studies/task24c_protocol.py)

Monte Carlo on the classical surrogate (catqubit.readout_protocol). Test set 200000
shots; thresholds and theta tuned on an independent training set of 100000 shots
(seeds [2024, 7000001]). Gamma_X source: ['ILLUSTRATIVE: Gamma_X(0) + linear-order drive term'].
Gamma_X(0) = {'2.1': 3.8495314808559236e-07, '1.2': 0.0005999198747807443, '1.4': 0.00012020004961271301} rad/us (bit_flip_rate, truncations {'2.1': {'na': 31, 'nb': 5, 'nb_extra': 6, 'na_taper': 13.2}, '1.2': {'na': 18, 'nb': 6, 'nb_extra': 0, 'na_taper': 1.0}, '1.4': {'na': 20, 'nb': 6, 'nb_extra': 0, 'na_taper': 1.0}}).
Factor-2 convention: Gamma_X is the decay rate of Re<a>; one-way jump rate Gamma_X/2;
p_X(T) = (1 - exp(-Gamma_X T))/2. Homodyne; heterodyne halves eta and doubles every time below.
Errors below 1/200000 are not resolved; 95% Wilson intervals are in the JSON.

Operating point at alpha = 2.1 ("Vuillot point"): smallest A whose training error is at most
the bit-flip probability accumulated during the readout itself, p_X(mean T). Small-alpha demo
rows use target = the best boxcar error (at its optimal window) on training data.
"window" columns: shortest fixed window meeting
the same target on training data. Speedup xN = boxcar test window reaching the SAME test error
as the protocol, divided by the protocol's mean stopping time (D'Anjou's t_f / T).
Hard cap: 5000 steps = 15 / mu^2. Freeze stop: also stop once
|P(s_k=+|s0=+,y) - P(s_k=+|s0=-,y)| <= 0.01 (further data cannot inform s0).
Erasure: |log-odds at stop| < a_e or P(s_k != s0 | y) > theta; (A, a_e, theta) chosen on training
data to minimize mean time subject to p_error <= target and p_erasure <= 10
x target (assumed erasure budget, at most 0.25).
